detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 10 - (F1 1 + F2 2 + F3 0.5 + F4 0.5) = 6. F2 takes 2 because its reader consequence is data loss: the page's own directory tree names home/ as where memory and journal live, and four lines later told the reader that deleting that folder is the uninstall, with no warning, while the page it links to opens its uninstall with an Important callout saying exactly that this destroys your memory. F1 takes 1 because the page reassured a reader that lifecycle is not something to think about while omitting the one macOS-specific fact that makes the reassurance wrong, and the cost lands on the 8 GB machine this page documents as the floor. F3 and F4 take 0.5 each: verbatim self-repetition in the limits list, and a review date a month older than the body. After the checklist, remaining is F5 alone at 0.5, so 10 - 0.5 = 9.5, floored to 9. The cap would also have held the score at 9, because remaining[] and further_improvements are both non-empty. Delta +3. Three things carry no detraction by ruling rather than by judgment, and the score would be lower if they did: the absent persona surface section (S1, T36), the absent inline procedure, and the sources entry naming a page T16 retires. The two linter errors carry no detraction either, because the linter owns them; they were fixed because the dispatch directed it and because the corpus gate for this phase is zero errors.
detailed_review.what_worked: The reshape itself is sound and this review did not have to argue with it. The install procedure is gone, the page reads as one type rather than two, the salvaged passages landed where a reader would look for them, and the orphaned 'the right-click-Open step above' is repaired. On top of that: F2 turned the most dangerous sentence on the page into an accurate one, and a reader who acts on §What installing gives you now keeps their journal. F1 closes the gap that made §Start and stop the house quietly wrong for the platform it is written for, using wording already published at wiki/backend/native-runtime.md:68-71 rather than a new claim. F3 gives the limits section something to say. F4 makes the page's own metadata tell the truth about when it was last looked at. L1 clears both hard linter errors, which were the whole gap between this corpus and a zero-error gate. Two verifications the dispatch asked for both came back clean. The real-time factor matches its source exactly, figure, machine, date and the phrase 'tool-grounded reply', and the author was right to publish 0.961 rather than carry the rounded 0.96 and the looser 'in a real conversation' forward. All four promises made by the three links to wiki/installing.md are now kept by that page: the macOS requirements, the right-click-Open first launch, the plan screen, and a troubleshooting section whose named failures are connection, silent voice and an interrupted download. The two pages now divide the subject rather than duplicating it, since wiki/installing.md:218-221 points back here for the macOS install root.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: One open finding, F5, at 0.5: the page teaches the reader that the local server is called 'the house' and then calls it the backend twice, once in the first line of §What installing gives you and once inside the figure's CAPTURE spec. Beyond the score, three structural things are open and none of them is this page's fault. The persona surface section the platform-overview shape requires is absent, so the page never says what Hearth looks like on a Mac, and T36 owns it. §What installing gives you now carries three subjects (what lands on disk, what runs while Hearth is open, and how fast the voice is) and about 330 words, which wiki/style-guide.md:104-110 already counts as two sections; the F2 fix made it slightly longer. Extracting the tree and the port list needs a reference page that does not exist and a task that owns the Windows page as well. And the page's one performance claim rests on a single run recorded in a file that never publishes.
